audit.recode_to: no reclassification. Keep not determinable for the Glottolog-tree object (Shahpuri/Dhanni/Jatki Lahnda). Annotate: (i) identity/crosswalk note that ISO 639-3 pnb as used by Ethnologue and by Hussain et al. 2020 JIPA ('Punjabi (Western, ISO-639-3 pnb)') covers Majhi-type Pakistani Punjabi (Lahore, Faisalabad/Lyallpur, Gujranwala, Sahiwal), which Glottolog files under panj1256 (majh1252), not under west2386; (ii) cite Hussain et al. 2020 pp. 293-294 alongside Bashir & Conners 2019 pp. 50-52 in the secondary-stress rule as out-of-tree (in-ISO) evidence of the Panjabi quantity-sensitive rule that Varma 1936 p. 64 says Lahnda single-word stress 'agrees with'; (iii) roster note for the editor: panj1256 (Eastern Panjabi incl. Majhi/Lahore) has no row, so the Punjabi quantity-sensitive system is coded nowhere; the fix is a new panj1256 record (B&C 2019, Hussain et al. 2020, Bhatia 1993, Dhillon 2010), not a reclassify of west2386.

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every deciding quotation (Varma 1936 p. 64, p. 51, pp. 91-92; Wilson 1899 future-tense note) is verbatim in the scanned files we hold at the stated lines. For the narrow Glottolog-tree languoid nothing better was found (Glottolog lists only Wilson 1899, Bailey 1904, Mullick 2003; CrossRef/archive. Smirnov 1975 unseen;org, Open Library and Cambridge Core directly). (3) The risk is identity, not misquotation: west238

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Stress is not contrastive in Lyallpuri Punjabi. All words have at least one stressed syllable. Stress assignment is sensitive to syllable weight ... Three categories of syllable weight ... light (monomoraic: (C)V ...), heavy (bimoraic ...), and superheavy (trimoraic: (C)VC ... or (C)VCC ...). In disyllabic words, the leftmost superheavy syllable is stressed ... If there is no superheavy syllable, then the penultimate syllable is stressed. In trisyllabic words ... stress is always placed on the penultimate or antepenultimate syllable, but not on the final syllable.' Also: 'Tones always align w

sources.quote: Tones 'occur in stressed syllables only'; 'When several syllables normally having the same kind of tone come together, it is customary in rapid conversation to pronounce the tone only in the most strongly stressed syllables'; 'The mark ' means that the following syllable is stressed. It has been very sparingly used.' No placement rule. (Glottolog files Bailey's 1904 Wazirabad grammar under west2386, but Wazirabad/Gujranwala speech is Majhi-side; carried only as context.)
